- Model consistently underestimates prices during sharp upward trends, especially after spikes (e.g., 37.26 → 48.22).
- Overestimates early in the forecast horizon when prices are rising, then underestimates later as the trend stabilizes.
- Shows persistent downward bias in the middle of the forecast window, particularly after a spike.
- Fails to capture mean reversion after strong upward moves; tends to hold high forecasts even when true values start declining.
- Overshoots after initial spikes, then corrects downward — model lags in recognizing the peak and overreacts to subsequent corrections.
- Underestimates the magnitude of price increases in the first 5–10 days of a new trend, then gradually adjusts upward.
- Model exhibits “late correction” bias — true values often exceed forecasts by 1–2 days after a spike, suggesting a lag in recognizing momentum.
- Forecasts are too smooth; fail to capture volatility clustering or sudden reversals in price direction.
